paper_citation.title: A multi-centre, multi-device benchmark dataset for landmark-based comprehensive fetal biometry
paper_citation.caption_quote: measurement error normalised by inter-landmark distance

analysis.identity_of_reported_numbers: Our reported numbers (0.0731 on v3_full test and 0.0808 on OOF 642) correspond strictly to Definition (i): Landmark Euclidean Coordinate Error normalized by GT inter-landmark distance. Specifically: 0.5 * (mean(||p_tad - g_tad||) / L_tad + mean(||p_apad - g_apad||) / L_apad).
analysis.explanation_of_0_0163_0_0242: Under Definition (ii) (|measured length error| / GT length), caliper relative errors are 0.0234 +- 0.0190 (TAD) and 0.0259 +- 0.0222 (APAD) on test, averaging 0.0247. When endpoints deviate in opposite perpendicular directions, their coordinate distance errors add up under Euclidean vector distance (giving ~0.073 - 0.080), but caliper length errors largely cancel, yielding relative caliper errors around 0.016 - 0.025. arXiv:2512.16710 Table 2 presents landmark NME around ~0.07-0.08 for BiometryNet, but relative length errors in other tables/benchmarks fall in the 0.0163 - 0.0242 regime.
analysis.direct_comparability: Our reported NME (0.0731 test, 0.0808 OOF) is directly comparable to BiometryNet's landmark NME (Table 2 M-C -> M-C: TAD 0.08 +- 0.08, APAD 0.07 +- 0.08). It is NOT directly comparable to scalar relative caliper measurement errors (0.016 - 0.024), which represent 1D length discrepancies rather than 2D coordinate localization.
